outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Introduction to Efficient LLM Finetuning
outline.description: This chapter establishes the motivation for QLoRA by contrasting the high memory costs of traditional full finetuning with the emerging need for accessible, large-scale model adaptation. It defines the problem space of training massive models on consumer hardware and introduces the core thesis: that 4-bit quantization combined with parameter-efficient methods can achieve parity with 16-bit full finetuning.
subtopics: The scalability crisis in LLM finetuning: Memory requirements of 16-bit training
Limitations of existing quantization methods (inference-only vs. training)
Overview of Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) and LoRA basics
The QLoRA proposition: Finetuning 65B models on a single 48GB GPU
Case Study Preview: The Guanaco Model Family and ChatGPT Performance Parity

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Mathematical Foundations of Quantization and Adapters
outline.description: Before diving into QLoRA specifics, this chapter reviews the necessary background concepts. It covers block-wise quantization mechanics, the challenges of outliers, and the mathematical formulation of Low-Rank Adapters (LoRA). It also analyzes the specific memory bottlenecks in training loops, highlighting why activation gradients dominate memory usage rather than adapter weights.
subtopics: Block-wise k-bit Quantization: Scaling, Rescaling, and Outlier Handling
Formalizing Low-Rank Adapters (LoRA): Factorized Projections ($	ext{XL}_1	ext{L}_2$)
Memory Footprint Analysis: Activations vs. Parameters vs. Optimizer States
The Role of Gradient Checkpointing in Memory Management
Why standard LoRA hyperparameters often fail to match full finetuning performance

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Core Innovations of QLoRA Architecture
outline.description: This is the technical heart of the textbook, detailing the three specific innovations that make QLoRA possible. It explains the statistical derivation of NF4, the recursive logic of Double Quantization, and the system-level engineering of Paged Optimizers.
subtopics: **4-bit NormalFloat **(NF4): Information-theoretic optimality for Gaussian-weighted distributions
**Double Quantization**: Reducing overhead by quantizing quantization constants ($c_2$)
**Paged Optimizers**: Leveraging NVIDIA Unified Memory to handle optimizer state paging between CPU/GPU
The Forward Pass Workflow: Dequantization to BF16 for Computation
The Backward Pass Workflow: Gradient flow through frozen quantized weights into LoRA adapters

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 4: Empirical Validation Against Standard Finetuning
outline.description: This chapter presents rigorous experimental evidence comparing QLoRA against full 16-bit finetuning and standard LoRA. It addresses skepticism regarding precision loss by demonstrating performance recovery across various architectures (RoBERTa, T5, LLaMA) and benchmarks (GLUE, MMLU). It also validates the superiority of NF4 over standard FP4/Int4.
subtopics: Experimental Design: Architectures ranging from Encoder-Decoder to Decoder-Only models
"Recovering" Lost Precision: Comparing 4-bit QLoRA vs. 16-bit Full Finetuning on GLUE/Super-NaturalInstructions
"Scaling Laws" Revisited: Matching 16-bit LoRA performance at 7B–65B scales on MMLU
`NF4` vs. `FP4` vs. `Int4`: Quantitative analysis of perplexity and accuracy retention
`Double Quantization` Impact: Verifying memory savings without accuracy degradation
